system.name: Dandelion
system.one_liner: an elastic cloud-native platform that executes applications as DAGs of pure compute and communication functions in sandboxes that cold-start in hundreds of microseconds

components.name: Frontend
components.role: manages client communication, handles registration/invocation requests, forwards to the dispatcher

components.name: Dispatcher
components.role: orchestrates function execution, tracks resources and the DAG registry, schedules ready functions

components.name: Waiting Functions
components.role: functions not yet ready because their input dependencies are unmet

components.name: Function / DAG Registry
components.role: registry of registered composition DAGs, function binaries, and metadata

components.name: Task Queues
components.role: type-specific queues (compute, communication) the dispatcher enqueues ready functions into

components.name: Control Plane
components.role: dynamically balances CPU resources between compute and communication engines using a PI controller

components.name: Comp. Engines
components.role: securely execute untrusted compute functions in isolated sandboxes, one task at a time per engine

components.name: Comm. Engines
components.role: handle interactions with external services (e.g., HTTP) using cooperative green threads, not sandboxed

components.name: Context
components.role: isolated memory context prepared per function for execution on an engine

flows.what: client HTTP requests for composition/function registration and invocation
compute tasks dequeued for isolated execution
communication tasks dequeued for external I/O
CPU core reassignment based on queue growth rates

content.key_idea: shows how the dispatcher schedules ready functions from a DAG into typed compute or communication engine queues, while a control-plane PI controller dynamically rebalances CPU cores between the two engine types for elasticity

summary: Dandelion is an elastic cloud-native platform that executes applications as DAGs of pure compute and communication functions in sandboxes that cold-start in hundreds of microseconds. Figure 4 shows a Dandelion worker node's architecture: an HTTP Frontend forwards client requests to a Dispatcher, which tracks a Function/DAG Registry and each function's input/output dependencies in its Waiting Functions queue. Ready functions are enqueued into typed Task Queues and dequeued by Compute Engines (pink, executing untrusted code in isolated per-engine Contexts) or Communication Engines (purple, handling external I/O with green threads, not sandboxed). A Control Plane monitors queue growth rates and reassigns CPU cores between the compute and communication engine pools using a PI controller, drawn as a feedback loop beneath the two engine types. Distinct fill colors separate the frontend, scheduling, and the two engine paths.
summary_zh: 图4展示Dandelion工作节点架构：前端转发请求给调度器，按依赖关系将就绪函数送入计算/通信两类任务队列与引擎，控制平面通过PI控制器在两类引擎间动态调度CPU核心。
